A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIRECT study. All 18 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original classification accuracy and minority-annotation results from ResNet-18 and LabelBench experiments under class imbalance and label noise.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain those original experiments. Appendix C additionally reports qualitative runtime comparisons and approximate trial durations.

M1.justification: The two-phase DIRECT procedure and VReduce remain. However, Algorithm 1 corrects cancelling threshold-count terms to class-k versus non-k counts, and Section 4.1 reverses the written margin from max(p)-p_k to p_k-max(p). These change the stated specification; the latter conflicts with the retained ordering convention. Implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten settings in Table 1: eight imbalanced variants of CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and PathMNIST, plus FMoW and iWildCam. The evaluated noise scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding noiseless, noisy, and LabelBench plots, including their differing baseline subsets. The added citation to Soltani et al. does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, class grouping, models, metrics, noise generation, and reported annotation batch sizes remain unchanged. Moving the setup to Appendix D and clarifying that loss weighting and smoothing apply to all algorithms do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The noise-level sweep, parallel-batch comparisons, and minority-annotation analyses are retained. The new theorem and complexity derivations do not add an ablation, robustness experiment, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over four trials with shaded standard errors. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: All existing benchmark and minority-annotation plots are retained with unchanged plotted results. Appendix C newly states that DIRECT was faster than BADGE and GALAXY in all experiments and reports approximate trial durations; these are additional runtime findings, not accuracy improvements.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained equivalence proof in Appendix A, v3 adds Theorem B.1 and its proof bounding GALAXY's probability of finding additional cuts under independent label flips. Appendix C adds complexity derivations and comparisons. Definition 4.1 also corrects the right-side class-count expression and includes threshold index zero.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: a one-dimensional reduction addressing imbalance and label noise, parallel annotation, and annotation savings exceeding 60% against leading methods and 80% against random sampling.

C2.justification: v3 adds a budget-dependent interpretation of GALAXY's spurious cuts and discusses neural-network costs dominating runtime. Its DIRECT error-decay discussion no longer explicitly states v2's benign-noise qualification. Appendix B also describes success-probability decay, contradicting the error-probability decay stated in Section 4.2.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses NVIDIA 3090 Ti GPUs, trial durations below two hours for ResNet-18 and roughly twelve hours for LabelBench, cumulative-sum computation, and possible CPU parallelization. Appendix D clarifies shared weighting and smoothing across algorithms. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated setting changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Soltani et al. on active learning for wireless communications and emphasizes the difficulty of applying classical agnostic learning to complex deep models. LabelBench and algorithm-selection references receive publication updates but represent retained works.

P1.justification: The introduction, discussion of existing algorithms in Section 3.2, and algorithm explanation are substantially rewritten. Related-work subsections are reordered, experimental setup moves to Appendix D, results move from Appendix B to E, and the impact statement moves to Appendix F.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 2's panels become side by side, algorithms receive full-width placements, Table 1 relocates to the appendix, and a new multiclass schematic appears as Figure 3. Existing result plots are resized and relocated without changed data.

improvement.justification: v3 improves exposition, corrects threshold expressions, and adds theoretical and reproducibility information while preserving the empirical evidence. However, its reversed margin sign conflicts with the retained ascending, class-k-on-the-left construction, and Appendix B contradicts Section 4.2 about success versus error probability decay. These technical inconsistencies offset the documentation gains sufficiently that a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
